added_failures_note: both arms read: the base suite 58 passed EXIT=0 and the after suite 61 passed EXIT=0, so the head arm added no failing test; the reviewed manifest names its logs only under the scratch directory its own cleanup removed, so those summary lines were read from the run's transcript and from the landed evidence fragment.
call_sites: reckon/crew/runs.py:1185 read_pointer -> crew stop, crew discard, recovery_liveness

findings.text: station_pid_on_this_host duplicates the station-lease reader the repository owns in reckon/crew/host_lease.py, whose HostLease.holder reads the same leases/station.json and whose process_runs_here owns the pid-plus-start-tick match, so two readers of one lease format can drift.

the start-tick comparison drops the pid_namespace the station lease records and that host_lease.process_runs_here requires, so a reader in another pid namespace (every crew worker runs under bwrap --unshare-pid) matches the station by pid number alone, and the guard can fail open or mistake another process for the station.
assert taken.attempt >= 1 cannot fail for any reservation the code returns, so it guards nothing and reads as coverage the case does not have.

the fixture builds the lease's pid_start with runs._process_start_time, the same reader the guard compares against, so the setup and the check move together and a regression inside that helper leaves every case green.

every test_logs and negative_control_log path lies under the run's own /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch directory, which the scratch cleanup removed, so a reviewer or a promotion reader cannot open the arms the record rests on.
changed_paths and retry_failures are written on one line, so changed_paths swallows the retry_failures key and a reader parsing changed_paths gets a value with the next field appended.
